items.note: S1.3.1 states the lemma faithfully: eight rows, arbitrary scratch values, three stages giving (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) with scratch restored. It is an infer step and gives neither the net-change identity (JV+RG)x nor the central/side coefficient cancellation, so it is not derived.

S1.3.2 gives the per-vertex frames, the commutation of a common frame with a pointwise gate, the operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and that only endpoint frames matter, all as in the paper. It is quoted, not derived through the invariant argument.

Nested labels from triple indicator vectors, the only decreasing edges (central wires from time 3 to 4, losing h) and L=Ich are correct, and L_b/N=100/539 appears in S1.3.4. The plan omits that neighbouring triple lines are orthogonal (what makes the nesting possible) and never gives the label budget Wm-2N+2L; it gives only the bit edge-rank sum.

S1.3.5 states the projections, the endpoint identity I_m and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m correctly, and S1.3 follows the paper's route (scratch network, frames, labels, rank sum). Two essential steps are missing: rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, and the source exception 2P_{U_a} of rank one, which turns -2N into -N.

S2.1 correctly gives one kernel aI+bX_v (or its inverse) per orthonormal residual vector and s_c<W_c m. It says telescoping gives C^{tensor m} on every role but drops the paper's conditions: only after the source and sink diagonal corrections and after undoing the signed exchange. The exact count s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c is not given.

L<N/2, s<Wm, deficits above 20*2^{-50}, and s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50} for both networks are all stated correctly. The exact eta values and the log m<20 step are omitted, but they are not claimed wrongly.

S1.1 lists the digit split, digit move and cyclic row split at O(V). S1.2 states the controlled update and unit scaling at O(V) but drops the hypothesis that the offset can be prepared in b^{O(1)} time (and the conditions on the prime q), which the paper's bound requires.

The factorization and the a-interchange shear are stated correctly, and S1.4.2 follows the paper's order (E_2 on D, E_1^{-1} on H, add Pi D, undo). Missing: the elimination proof of the factorization, and the three-update gadget D_j+=H_i, swap, D_j=H_i-D_j that turns each one of Pi into a single interchange; the plan only asserts it.

The sub-steps reproduce the paper's proof: cyclic row split into W role streams, shear frames giving H<-H+D on every row (scratch rows included), the three-update interchange, the recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) solving to O(e^tau), and the parking-stack schedule at O(V) per node.

The steps follow the proof: top rho=O(log e) digits used as the row field and padded to a multiple of W^k, base-m pieces handed to the power-width procedure, and binary ranges padded to [q^e] at a fixed volume factor.

S2.2 states exactly s_c child calls on f=e/m axes plus a fixed number of binary row additions, and S2.3 gives H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D, both correctly. The mechanism is missing: the conjugation by P_M that moves the residual directions into slots, and the inverse-child identity (C^{-1})^{tensor f}=(-i)^f Z C Z.

The route matches the paper: eight controlled additions that flip parity and restore w, a bad set of guards near the range ends with |B|<=delta_bad M, and a stable-radix-sort repair. The statement keeps only K/log p->infinity, dropping the paper's other family conditions (A_rect=O(p), R superpolynomial, f<=d<=p) and the explicit cost formula. The derivation leaves implicit why T_0S_0^{-1} permutes B.

Row index from O(log d) chunks, the u=Wg+w split giving V/W children, the recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), and the base-m pieces all match. The plan omits the leaf cutoff e<d^beta with F(e)=O(e), the overhead bound via K<=e^{c/beta}, and the internal and leaf sums. It also replaces the condition max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}<lambda' with 'a fixed lambda'<1'.

S2 and its sub-steps follow the paper's route: phase kernel, recursion, packed basis changes, recurrence, guard widths with Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1})=o(p), and one final truncation. The statement omits the parameter bands on d and r and the exponent conditions. The derivation omits the arithmetic-depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E behind the guard width, and the check that every packed call meets the lemma's hypotheses.

S3.1 gives B_tF_t^- and F_t^+B_t^{-1}. The S3.2 sub-steps reproduce the layout cost terms (O(TpdK), O(Tp pK^{tau-1}), O(Tp l d^{lambda'})) and the single-truncation error argument. Not stated: character cancellation F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I, and the full counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1} with the layout permutation. The bit-reversed order is not derived.
S3.3 gives four signed products at evaluation point 2^{4p}, centered extraction, negacyclic wrap, Q_p(fg/r) and O(rp log(rp)), matching the lemma. It gives no derivation.

The procedure (retained LB order, pointwise packed products, opposite transform, scale by M) and the error and cost match. S3 calls the result 'cyclic convolution' without the normalization (f*g)/(rM). The derivation omits the normalization identity F^-(f*g)=M(F^-f)(F^-g) and only gestures at the 3delta+eta error accounting.

The one-dimensional identity, the tensor identity, the linewise implementation with at most T/t_i lines, and the axis exposure at O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)) are all stated correctly, and the tensor/implementation part follows the proof. The construction of A and B_0 and the proof of P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA (lines 3576-3792) are taken as given.

S5.8 states the source-permutation cancellation (RF^+_s)[(RF_s u)(RF_s v)]=(u*v)/S^2 exactly. The chirp half is only referred to as 'the chirp identity': the chirp a_j=exp(-pi i sum s_i j_i^2/t_i) and the formula QF_t u = conj(a)(a*(conj(a)u))/T are never given.

The fixed exponents, the sizes b, p, d, K and T, the prime intervals, T/2<S<T and the n^{o(1)} search all match the paper. The plan never defines eta (=1/(4d)), alpha or gamma, so 'room for resampling' (alpha^4 theta_i>p) is not made concrete.
The algebra isomorphism x->prod x_i^{mu_i}, preservation of convolution and the cost are correct. mu_i=P_i^{-1} mod s_i is left undefined and the triangular digit formula is only named.
S5.5.1 states the twist isomorphism and the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j correctly. It does not state the resulting formula M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g).

The source transform (A, chirp transform, B_0, scale 2^gamma, counterpart RF_s) and the six-step algorithm with scalings by S and 2^{2b+4}S follow the paper. S5.8 explains the two S factors. The digit scale 2^{-b-2} and the definition of F^+ by conjugation are left implicit.

The chain E_ring=M(3L+2)<5TL (norm <.701), chirp error <8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL (norm <.501), E_w<28*2^gamma T^2L, the final bound 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2, and carries <Q_0^2 all match the paper's error budget step by step.

The table powers, the margins with min g_i=2^{-181}=2kappa, the per-row justifications, the o(Tp) setup and exceptional sorting, and the final O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) with a schoolbook cutoff all reproduce the paper.

S0 says the bound refutes the n log n optimality conjecture in this model. It does not give the content: the eventual lower bound T_A(n)>=c_A n lg n, its negation by liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n)=0, and that the bound gives limit zero.

errors.says: There is a fixed network of W XOR gates on wires ...
errors.paper: W is the number of wires (W_b=2N+I(vz_b+c_b)); the network has at most 12W gates, and the proposition reads 'The bit network has W_b wires, uses only pointwise XOR gates'.

errors.says: Cyclic convolution of arrays over C[y]/(y^r+1) ... is computed ... with error below sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p}.
errors.paper: The procedure approximates the normalized convolution M_r(f,g)=(f*g)/(rM), and the error bound is for that normalized quantity.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound: bit network and frames to address interchange, complex phase network to simultaneous butterfly layers, then synthetic transforms, ring convolution, Gaussian resampling with retained permutations, CRT layout, exact recovery, and a time table whose minimum margin is 2^{-181}=2kappa. It thins out in the finite-network constructions (the rank/dimension link and the source-rank correction behind s_b, the P_M conjugation behind the phase recursion), in the one-dimensional Gaussian resampling construction, and in the chirp identity, all of which are asserted rather than shown. The recurrence-unrolling conditions that fix lambda' are also not carried, though none of these gaps breaks the chain.
